{
  "research_question": "Do the effects of stimulation paradigm on mouse navigation performance differ statistically across the five conditions (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) for Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": [
    "Combined",
    "ICMS Only",
    "Dim Visual Only",
    "Bright Visual Only",
    "Sham"
  ],
  "response_variables": [
    "Time-to-Target",
    "Success",
    "Path Efficiency",
    "Average Speed",
    "AD"
  ],
  "anova_plan": [
    "For each response variable, fit a one-way ANOVA model: Response ~ Stim_Paradigm.",
    "For Time-to-Target, Average Speed, AD (continuous, approximately normal distribution described in summary), use standard F-test ANOVA.",
    "For Success (binary, 0/1), ordinary least squares ANOVA may violate homoscedasticity due to varying binomial variances per group; consider a Generalized Linear Model (GLM) with binomial link and robust standard errors or Beta regression for continuous interpretation, or use ANOVA with cautioned inference given unbalanced groups (n ranges from 3323 to 48846).",
    "For Path Efficiency (bounded 0-max, mean 0.47, high skew implied by max 29.81 vs mean 0.47), check normality heavily; if distribution is heavily right-skewed or non-normal, prefer Box-Cox transformation or a robust permutation ANOVA.",
    "Check overall significance (F-statistic) for each variable against alpha=0.05."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence of observations: Verify experiment design ensures separate trials/mice do not induce non-independence (leverage context of 'mouse_navigation' with 8 mouse levels; if multiple trials per mouse, treat Mouse as a random factor via Mixed Model ANOVA instead of one-way ANOVA).",
    "Normality: Inspect residuals for each group for normality (Q-Q plots, Shapiro-Wilk) using summary stats (Time-to-Target skew likely positive given min 0.5/max 201).",
    "Homogeneity of Variances: Check Levene's test or Bartlett's test for equal variances across the 5 paradigms, crucial given large sample size differences (n=3323 vs n=48846) which can inflate Type I error in standard ANOVA.",
    "Linearity/Correct Model specification: Ensure additivity of main effect."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus ANOVA F-test is significant (p < 0.05) for a variable:",
    "Perform pairwise comparisons between all 5 stim paradigms.",
    "Apply Tukey's Honestly Significant Difference (HSD) correction for multiple comparisons to control Family-Wise Error Rate.",
    "Calculate effect sizes (eta-squared or partial omega-squared) for all significant contrasts.",
    "For Success variable specifically, use two-proportion z-tests or logistic regression contrasts instead of t-tests if variances are highly heterogeneous."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham group shows drastically lower Success (mean=0.27) compared to all stimulation groups (means ~0.67-0.78), suggesting a main effect on success.",
    "Sham group likely has superior performance (longer Time-to-Target, lower Success, lower Path Efficiency relative to stimulation groups) or conversely, stimulation virtue testing; specifically, Sham has longest Time-to-Target (4.68) vs Combined (2.56), suggesting stimulation improves speed to target.",
    "Sham group has lowest AD (0.236) vs others, which paradoxically might indicate lower dispersion (better performance) if AD is angular deviation from a straight line, or if AD is noise, it shows less randomness. Clarification needed on whether lower AD = better efficiency.",
    "Success rates are significantly different between Sham and all stimulated groups based on mean differences.",
    "Path Efficiency is lower in Sham (0.308) than stimulated groups (~0.43-0.50), suggesting a potential effect paradigm."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Unbalanced design: Group sizes vary drastically (Sham n=3505 vs Combined n=48846), reducing power for Sham group comparisons and violating ideal ANOVA assumptions unless weighted correction is used.",
    "Potential pseudoreplication: 'Mouse' has 8 levels with ~10k trials per mouse (approx). If data reflects multiple trials per mouse, standard ANOVA treats them as independent, inflating N and deflating variance; Mixed Effects Models with 'Mouse' as random intercept are required.",
    "Distributional violations: Time-to-Target (0 to 201) and Path Efficiency (0 to 29) likely violate normality assumptions for standard ANOVA without transformation.",
    "Binary nature of 'Success': Ordinary ANOVA assumes continuous interval data; binomial data violates this assumption though large N helps."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit Linear Mixed Effects Models (LME) for each response variable with Stim_Paradigm as fixed effect and Mouse as random intercept to account for repeated measures/trials within the same animal, replacing standard One-Way ANOVA to address pseudoreplication."
}
